---
id: SA-0308
title: A host-filed survivor's claim reaches the Disagreements row with nothing checking it arrived, so a build that dropped it would still pass
type: bug
priority: 3
touches:
  - tests/test_report.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/**
  - tests/test_next_id.py
  - tests/test_review.py
  - tests/test_session.py
budget_usd: 4
max_attempts: 2
max_turns: 30
estimated_lines: 32
estimate_measured: true
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `test_a_host_filed_survivor_outside_the_diff_is_reported_as_a_blocker`
      (`tests/test_report.py:1257-1327`) builds its `survivor` `Finding` by
      hand, at lines 1265-1277, typing the exact sentence
      `survivor_finding`'s wrong-version branch writes
      (`saffron/phases/review.py:756-759`) rather than calling that
      function. Its own assertions on `row2` (lines 1319-1323) check the
      survivor's location, the implementer's argument and the critic's
      reason — never the claim `_disagreements` renders into that same row
      at `saffron/report/pr_body.py:379` (`f"| {_cell(finding.claim)} "`).
      The test instead builds `survivor` by calling `review.survivor_finding`
      itself, with a `Criterion` and a wrong version, exactly as
      `tests/test_review.py:2098-2130` already does, and asserts the string
      that call returns — `survivor.claim` — appears in `row2`. A row that
      drops, truncates or substitutes that claim fails the new assertion;
      today's row, which renders it verbatim, passes.
    witness: tests/test_report.py::test_a_host_filed_survivor_outside_the_diff_is_reported_as_a_blocker
---

## Context

Follow-up to `SA-0299` (#edc692f0), from the join lens's end-review of this
stack (ADR 7, backlog item b-792ab2). The findings below were filed against
the origin head `edc692f0`; two of three no longer hold at the top of this
stack, `52bad63b`.

**Two of the three findings are already fixed.** Both cite
`tests/test_report.py:417`, the docstring of
`test_findings_that_never_anchored_are_named_as_never_adjudicated`. At
`edc692f0` it still read "`anchored_blockers` and `anchored_concerns` both
filter on the anchor," which `SA-0299`'s own notes had already flagged as
turning false for `anchored_blockers`. The review commit `29404778` (between
`edc692f0` and this stack's head) rewrote it to "Both rules filter a lens's
finding on the anchor... Only a host-filed survivor reaches REBUT
unanchored" (`tests/test_report.py:417-420`, read at `52bad63b`). Nothing
here repeats that edit.

**The third finding still holds.** `survivor_finding`
(`saffron/phases/review.py:736-769`) writes the same `HOST_FILED` bracket,
`"[host-filed criterion probe] "` (`saffron/phases/review.py:56`), whether
`version` is `None` (line 750) or names a wrong version (line 756). A wrong
version's survivor therefore opens with a mark that names the wrong kind of
edit — "criterion probe" and "wrong version" are the two terms DESIGN.md §4
keeps apart (`DESIGN.md:1118`, `DESIGN.md:1127`). Before `SA-0299`,
`anchored_blockers` dropped an unanchored survivor, so this mislabel never
left `findings.json`. `SA-0299` made an unanchored survivor a blocker, so it
now reaches `_disagreements` (`saffron/report/pr_body.py:311-379`) and is
rendered into the pull request's Disagreements table, at the claim column
`_cell(finding.claim)` produces (`saffron/report/pr_body.py:379`).

**Why this spec does not rename `HOST_FILED`.** That edit is in
`saffron/phases/review.py`, which lies outside this follow-up's allowed
paths. `follow_up.write_follow_ups` computes those paths as the finding's own
file plus every test path the stack's range changed
(`saffron/follow_up.py:304-306`); the join lens anchored this finding at
`tests/test_report.py`, not at `saffron/phases/review.py`, so that is the
only file this spec may touch. The vocabulary fix is left for a spec scoped
with `saffron/phases/review.py` in its own `touches`.

## Problem

1. **The gap this spec closes.** The one test that renders a host-filed
   survivor into the Disagreements table
   (`tests/test_report.py:1257-1327`) hand-types a `claim` string that
   happens to match what `survivor_finding` produces today
   (`saffron/phases/review.py:756-759`), then never checks that string, or
   any fragment unique to it, against the rendered row
   (`tests/test_report.py:1319-1323` checks only the file:line, the
   rebuttal's argument and the verdict's reason). Two problems follow from
   the same cause. First, nothing ties the fixture to the real function, so
   a change to `survivor_finding`'s wording — including the vocabulary fix
   this spec defers — could drift from this test's fixture with no
   failure here to catch it. Second, nothing here confirms that
   `_disagreements` actually renders the claim at all: a build that dropped,
   truncated or substituted the claim column would still pass today's
   assertions, silently hiding the very text an operator needs to judge a
   host-filed survivor's claim (`DESIGN.md §5.5`, `SA-0299`'s own motivation).

2. **The fix.** The test builds `survivor` through
   `review.survivor_finding(criterion, edit, content, version=...)` —
   already imported in this file's sibling, `tests/test_review.py:2098-2130`
   — rather than a hand-written `Finding(...)`. It then asserts
   `survivor.claim in row2`, alongside the existing checks.

## Out of scope

- **Splitting `HOST_FILED` into a criterion-probe mark and a wrong-version
  mark.** The real fix, in `saffron/phases/review.py:56,750,756`, is outside
  this follow-up's allowed paths (`saffron/follow_up.py:304-306`). Left for a
  spec whose `touches` names that file.
- **`tests/test_review.py:2098-2130`'s own pin of the exact `HOST_FILED`
  text.** It already asserts `survivor_finding`'s claim character for
  character for both forms; this spec changes nothing there, and does not
  touch `tests/test_review.py` (`forbidden`, above).
- **The already-fixed docstring at `tests/test_report.py:417-420`.** Resolved
  by `29404778` before this stack's head; see Context.

## Notes for the agent

**Build the fixture exactly as `tests/test_review.py` does.** Import
`Criterion, Mutant` from `saffron.intake` alongside the existing
`parse_spec` import (`tests/test_report.py:12`), and `survivor_finding`
from `saffron.phases.review` in place of `HOST_FILED`
(`tests/test_report.py:20`) — nothing else in this file still needs
`HOST_FILED` once the hand-built `Finding` is gone; keep the import list
one that `ruff` accepts with no unused name. Declare one `Criterion` (any
`claim`, witness `"t.py::a"`) and one `Mutant` on
`file="saffron/gates/runner.py"`, `find="RESULT = CANNED"`. Put `edit.find`
on line 330 the same way `tests/test_session.py`'s own survivor fixtures do
— 329 filler lines, `f"line {n}" for n in range(1, 330)`, then
`"RESULT = CANNED\n"` — so `survivor.line == 330` matches every other
assertion in this test untouched. Call `survivor_finding(criterion, edit,
content, version="the guard is removed")`. Leave every other line of the
test as it is: the two `_finding(...)` calls, the `reviews` list, the
`RebutResult`, the render call, the row extraction, and the `## Not
covered` assertions all read `survivor` the same way whether it was built
by hand or by the function.

**Measured on a prototype at this stack's head.** The whole change is one
file, 15 insertions and 17 deletions (32 changed lines), 94 changed tokens
by the `size` gate's own counter — 7% of the `bug` ceiling of 1300. `ruff
check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the result. The witness fails
with the source reverted (the removed `survivor.claim in row2` line never
ran) and passes once the change lands; the rest of `tests/test_report.py`
(97 tests) stays green throughout.

Commit after the witness passes. Uncommitted work dies with the cell.
